title: Felix Respect Beat
prompt:
Felix looks at Byleth with reluctant respect, guarded but no longer dismissive. The change is subtle: a held gaze, a small breath, no smile. Byleth remains neutral and does not seek praise.

Youth/beauty guard: Keep academy students youthful, attractive, clean-skinned and official-game-inspired. For war phase students, keep them early-20s and beautiful; show pressure through costume, posture, lighting and setting, not through aging.

Cinematic continuity: Block=Mock Battle. Transition in: Felix held gaze after exercise. Transition out: cut to Dimitri hand/face dark-line. Screen/camera rule: left-to-right tactical geography; action returns to Byleth as anchor. Audio bridge: whistle, training weapons, bowstring, controlled breaths. Generate with 2s editorial handle where possible; begin and end with usable motion, not a frozen poster. Maintain direction, eyelines, and spatial geography from adjacent shots.

Camera: medium close hold, slight rack focus from Byleth to Felix.

Scene09 production gate: do not generate final video from the blocked source image if it is SVG or legacy training-yard raster. Use production_image_path after a real cinematic raster keyframe is generated and QA-approved.
Character continuity gate: every named character must match the listed selected.png reference assets for face, hair, age, costume silhouette, and color accents.
negative_prompt: No game UI, no subtitles, no readable text, no watermark, no modern objects. No identity drift, face swaps, costume drift, extra limbs, warped hands, flickering faces, or sudden style changes. Avoid: friendly smile, exaggerated nod, adult hardboiled styling. No middle-aged face unless canonically required, no old face, no wrinkles, no tired eye bags, no harsh pores, no weathered skin, no gaunt face, no matronly look, no gritty realism, no generic medieval extra. Keep academy students youthful, attractive, clean-skinned and official-game-inspired; for war phase students, keep them early-20s and beautiful, showing war pressure through costume, posture, lighting and setting, not through aging.
